why_ai: Licensed masters and engineers move cargo across oceans on ships, and carriers carry Hague-Visby liability; autonomy will not crew deep-sea ships by 2031.
why_clarity: Cargo is delivered on schedule or not and slot revenue is known within days, though network and pricing calls are judged by feel.
why_digital: Bookings and documents are digital and buyers book carriers worldwide, but the product is physical carriage on ships.

why_ai: Allocation and pricing are screen work that models can support, though key-account relationships and adversarial rate calls keep humans in the loop.
why_clarity: Net revenue per slot is measured every sailing, but trade managers set overbooking by feel with no written method.
why_digital: Bookings, rates and load data in, prices and allocations out, all on screens; contracts still negotiated with customers in person.

why_ai: Fixtures are negotiated through trusted broker relationships on novel ship-cargo pairs, but position matching and estimates automate.
why_clarity: TCE against the Baltic route average is a clear score, but each fixture is a different ship, cargo and port pair settled weeks later.
why_digital: Broker emails and estimates on screens, contracts by email and phone across borders.

why_ai: Rule-bound aggregation of fuel data into regulated reports is what software does best; verifiers keep a signature step.
why_clarity: Approved monitoring plans fix the method, every ship reports every year, and verifiers accept or correct before 31 March.
why_digital: Noon reports and delivery notes in, digital reports to EU and IMO systems out; services bought remotely.

why_ai: Claims analysis automates, but settlement negotiation and litigation calls stay adversarial and human.
why_clarity: Time bars and liability rules are codified and claims recur by type, though outcomes settle months later.
why_digital: Survey reports and photos of physical damage in, digital claim files out, handled remotely with correspondents.

why_ai: US-crewed ships physically carry cargo under protected-trade law, and government relationships matter.
why_clarity: Sailings and programme compliance are measurable and recur weekly, though fleet economics depend on policy.
why_digital: Physical carriage by US-flag ships; bookings and tenders arrive digitally from US buyers.

why_ai: Island freight moves on US-built ships with US crews, and island shippers stay with carriers they trust.
why_clarity: Containers land on the scheduled day or not, week after week, with feedback at each arrival.
why_digital: Physical carriage to islands; customers are local retailers and distributors in Hawaii, Alaska and Puerto Rico.

why_ai: US-crewed ships carry government cargo under preference law; demand depends on statute and appropriations rather than AI.
why_clarity: Tender awards and eligibility are definite, but each tender's route and timing differ.
why_digital: Tenders arrive digitally from US agencies, while the service is physical sealift.

why_ai: Licensed officers personally keep ships safe at sea and sign statutory records, with consequential judgement.
why_clarity: Record-keeping rules are codified and inspections give pass or fail, but seamanship and engineering calls vary.
why_digital: Work happens on ships at sea; reporting is the digital part and crewing is arranged through managers and unions.

why_ai: Turning instructions into bills of lading is extraction and validation, which agents absorb directly.
why_clarity: Each bill is right or amended, across millions of near-identical cases, with instant comparison to the issued bill.
why_digital: Emails and PDFs in, structured bills and eBLs out, produced in offshore centres for global customers.

why_ai: Clock reconstruction and invoice assembly are rules over event data that software takes over.
why_clarity: The FMC rule defines the elements and windows, charges recur daily, and disputes settle within 30 days.
why_digital: Container events in, invoices and dispute replies out, entirely digital.

why_ai: Fleet databases and forecasts are data work AI tooling speeds up, though the houses' reputations and analyst calls keep buyers.
why_clarity: Registers are exact, but forecasts are judged against deliveries and markets months later.
why_digital: Registries and broker data in, subscriptions and reports out, sold worldwide online.

why_ai: Lenders still want named independent valuers on certificates, but model values cover much of the routine work.
why_clarity: Each certificate is a defined number checked against later sales, repeated across fleets each test date.
why_digital: Transaction and AIS data in, certificates and online values out, sold to global lenders.

why_ai: Panel assessments are rule-based and increasingly data-driven, though settlement use keeps trusted publishers.
why_clarity: Methodologies are published and routes assessed daily, checked against fixtures over time.
why_digital: Broker assessments in, indices and licences out, distributed globally.

why_ai: Market commentary is easily generated, but brokers' client relationships keep the research attached to deals.
why_clarity: Weekly reports recur in a fixed shape, though their value is hard to measure.
why_digital: Fixture data in, reports out by email to clients worldwide.

why_ai: Mutual cover, member relationships and adversarial claims keep accountable humans central.
why_clarity: Premiums and claims follow rules, but large casualties are rare and resolve over years.
why_digital: Claims files and survey records in, cover and guidance out, through club offices and correspondents.

why_ai: Underwriting authority and war-risk calls in volatile areas remain human decisions backed by capital.
why_clarity: Rating rules exist, but hull losses are rare and war risk changes with events.
why_digital: Survey and claims data analysed on screens; cover placed through brokers in London and Oslo.

why_ai: Threat judgement in contested waters is adversarial and consequential, though open-source monitoring automates.
why_clarity: Assessments recur by area, but whether a warning was right is known only when incidents happen or not.
why_digital: Open sources and networks in, reports and alerts out, sold to global clients.

why_ai: Routing and performance modelling are computational work that AI-native weather models are already entering.
why_clarity: Every voyage is routed and evaluated the same way, with arrival and consumption known at voyage end.
why_digital: Weather data and noon reports in, digital advisories and reports out, sold worldwide.

why_ai: Report compilation automates, while accredited verifiers keep a signed step that persists.
why_clarity: Monitoring plans and EU rules fix the method; reports recur yearly per ship and are accepted or corrected.
why_digital: Operators' data in, verified reports out, all remote.

why_ai: Credit decisions carry bank accountability and borrower relationships; analysis tooling assists.
why_clarity: Covenants are defined, but credit outcomes resolve over the loan's life.
why_digital: Borrower data analysed on screens; loans arranged through relationship banking.

why_ai: The rules and advisory units counted here work on screens; the society's name and institutional accountability keep buyers, while surveying, the physical half, is excluded as production.
why_clarity: Rule development and advisory studies follow technical standards, but each study is bespoke and whether a rule or forecast was right shows only over years.
why_digital: Technical data, studies and rule texts in and out, with some site visits; advisory is sold to owners and yards worldwide.

why_ai: The central analytics team benchmarks managed fleets on screens; owner relationships and safety accountability keep some judgement human, but the analysis itself automates.
why_clarity: Fleet KPIs for cost, performance and safety are defined and recur monthly across hundreds of ships, though incident causes take time to establish.
why_digital: Ship data flows to shore systems and reports go to owners abroad; the analytics work is entirely on screens.

why_ai: Pricing and network calls are screen work with high stakes; models assist but carriers keep the decision.
why_clarity: Revenue and utilisation are measured every sailing, but methods vary by desk.
why_digital: Booking and network data in, rates and plans out, all internal and digital.

why_ai: Statutory enforcement and adjudication need accountable officials.
why_clarity: Rules are codified, but competition analysis and complaints are case by case and slow.
why_digital: Filings in, decisions out, within US jurisdiction.

why_ai: Laytime calculation and invoice audit are rule-bound document work that automates directly.
why_clarity: Charter party and tariff terms fix the calculation; thousands of claims recur with quick settlement.
why_digital: Documents in, calculations and claims out, done from offshore desks.

why_ai: Surveyors inspect damage on site and adjusters exercise accountable judgement on rare casualties.
why_clarity: Adjustment rules exist, but each casualty is different and resolves over years.
why_digital: Physical inspections plus document work, engaged case by case worldwide.

why_ai: Member representation and standard-setting depend on trust and politics rather than automatable work.
why_clarity: Outputs are negotiated positions and standards, with outcomes known slowly if at all.
why_digital: Policy and standards work on screens and in meetings at IMO and with members.

why_ai: Physical fuel delivery and sample testing persist; trading relationships matter at each port.
why_clarity: Specifications and tests are standard and recur with every delivery, checked quickly.
why_digital: Physical fuel and samples, traded and reported digitally across ports.

why_ai: Statutory programmes need accountable officials; payments and eligibility checks automate.
why_clarity: Programme rules are codified and cycles recur annually.
why_digital: Filings in, payments and determinations out, within US agencies.
